rules.statement: Do not add a `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` `FrameworkReference` to a low-level abstractions package; put the ASP.NET Core HTTP types (results, HTTP exceptions, URI descriptors) in a separate `*.AspNetCore.Abstractions` package and keep the base abstractions on the BCL alone.
rules.why: A FrameworkReference on the lowest common package pulls ASP.NET Core into everything that depends on it. It also stops framework-free branches such as crypto/JOSE from referencing the core without turning the layering upside down.
rules.check: Look for a `<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />` added to an `*.Abstractions` (or similarly low-tier) .csproj, or for ASP.NET Core types (IResult, HttpContext, etc.) added to a package meant to depend only on the BCL.

rules.statement: Put shared `JsonElement` helpers (such as `TryGetPropertyValue<T>`, `IsNullOrUndefined`, `OrEmptyObject`, `EmptyObject`) in `NCode.Json`'s `JsonElements` and use them from there, not from a package-specific `JsonElementExtensions` class.
rules.why: A single dependency-free home avoids keeping two copies of the same utility in separate branches.
rules.check: Look for new or existing local `JsonElement` extension/helper classes that duplicate what `NCode.Json.JsonElements` already provides.

rules.statement: When you need a detached `JsonElement` parsed from a string, use `JsonElement.Parse(string)`, not `JsonDocument.Parse(...)` followed by `RootElement.Clone()` or other hand-rolled variants.
rules.why: The ADR makes `JsonElement.Parse(string)` the standard way to do detached parsing.
rules.check: Look for `JsonDocument.Parse(json)` used only to get a cloned or detached root element, where `JsonElement.Parse` would work.

rules.statement: Declare a project or package reference directly in the project that consumes its types, rather than relying on it arriving transitively through another package that doesn't use it.
rules.why: A reference held by the wrong package is misplaced. It blocks refactoring dependency tiers, and removing it breaks downstream projects that were quietly depending on it.
rules.check: Look for a .csproj reference added to a package that doesn't use those types itself, or for code that uses types from an assembly its project doesn't reference directly.
